translation.en: The 5th chapter of the 4th Vaiśvadeva book of the Taittirīya Saṁhitā belonging to the Kṛṣṇa Yajurveda.
Salutations to the blessed Rudra.
Salutation to the Rudra’s furies, and to your beloved arrow (action) salutation. Salutation to your bow (aim) and salutation to your both arms.
That your arrow which is the most auspicious and auspicious is your bow. And with that auspicious quiver of yours o Rudra you make us happy.
O Rudra, your body that is auspicious is not terrifying and not evil looking. With that most peaceful body of yours become visible to us, o Lord of the mountains.
O Dweller in the mountains, the arrow you bear in your hand for shooting, o auspicious protector of the mountain, please make it not intend to harm people or herds.
We salute you with auspicious words, o mountain lord, so that for us the whole world may indeed be healthy and friendly.

text.en: in “jambhayant sarvāśca” the letter “t” is āgama, inserted letter, called abhinidhānaḥ (T. Pr. XIV. 9.)

translation.en: The protector and the first divine healer declared, that all snakes and all evil spirits are crushed.
That one who is copper-red, reddish as the dawn, that is brown, and auspicious, All these Rudras who are situated around in the thousands directions, we beg protection from their wrath.
That blue-throated and very red one who sneaks, the cowherds saw and the water-bearers saw Him, and Him having been seen by all the creatures grants us happiness.
Salutation to the blue-throated thousand-eyed bountiful one, and also to all those beings of his, to them I offered my salutations.
You loosen the bow string from both of the tips, and those arrows in your hand, o blessed one, may you throw them away.
Having unstrung the bow, you are a thousand-eyed owner of a hundred quivers, and having broken off the arrow tips, be auspicious and benevolent to us!
Unstrung is the bow of him with the matted hair, and pointless is the arrow, his arrows are lost, empty is his quiver.
O most generous one the arrow that was in your hand, and your bow, You are that one with freedom from disease, please protect us from all sides!
May there be salutations to you, the courageous one and to the unstrung weapon, and salutation to both of your hands and to your bow.
May the arrow from your bow avoid us from all sides, Likewise that quiver of yours, please place it there far from us.
Salutations to Śambhu.

Salutations to the revered Lord of the Universe, to the great God, to the three-eyed one, annihilator of Tripura, to the one who embodies the three fires and time, to Rudra as the fire of time, to the blue-throated one, to the conqueror of death, to the Lord of all, to the eternally auspicious one (to Śaṅkara, the giver of peace), to to the glorious and great god, salutations!
